subject: Account maturity & ML workload plan — Nimbus discovery recap
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Account maturity & ML workload plan — Nimbus discovery recap

Hi Dana / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the proposed next steps so we have the same playbook going into the pilot: 

High-level pain points you shared
- Sporadic P95 latency spikes on production reranking (observed up to ~700ms) impacting UX.
- Token burn on chat + reranking workflows causing monthly cost growth (~120M tokens/month today).
- KV cache thrash with long conversation histories (4k+ token windows) causing increased compute.
- Need to support a new near-real-time reranking endpoint (sub-200ms P95 target) for the recommendations product.

Goals you outlined
- Pilot a dedicated inference lane for reranking in Q2 to prove P95 reduction and unit cost stability.
- Keep primary chat traffic on hosted endpoint with caching improvements.
- Evaluate dedicated capacity (VPC/private routing) for Q3 rollout if pilot meets latency and cost SLOs.
- Minimal disruption to current infra and ability to pin model versions.

Proposed scope (what Redwood will deliver for the pilot)
- 6-week pilot: configure a dedicated pool (1 GPU slot initially), KV cache tuning and prefix caching, model quantization suggestions, and telemetry dashboard (per-route latency & cost).
- Success metrics: P95 <= 220ms for reranking; unit token cost change <= +10% vs current baseline; end-to-end error rate < 0.5%.

Next steps & owners
- Vanessa (Redwood): send mutual action plan and capacity options (attached). (Today)
- Dana (Nimbus): confirm pilot scope and any security checklist items (SOC2 details requested). (by 2027-02-17)
- Redwood infra (Marcus): produce T-shirt pricing and recommended commit levels for Dedicated tiers. (by 2027-02-16 EOD)
- Schedule technical kickoff and design call w/ Nimbus infra + product (proposed 2027-02-22).

Attachments: NIMBUS-MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan), redwood-capacity-options.pdf (capacity + pricing sketches)

If I've missed anything obvious, call it out and I'll update the MAP. If all looks good, I can lock the kickoff time and get Marcus looping in engineering for the design call.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Appreciate the detailed recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) SOC2 / security: please send the SOC2 report link or an attestation. Our InfoSec will also want to review network diagrams if we move to a VPC private deployment.
2) Pricing: can you provide a T-shirt pricing range for the pilot vs a Q3 Dedicated commit (ballpark numbers are fine).

Vanessa —

Draft pricing and capacity options below (ballpark, subject to infra sizing during kickoff):

Pilot Option (6-week):
- Dedicated pilot pool: 1x A100-equivalent GPU slot + tuned KV cache
- Managed telemetry & tuning: included
- Price: $8,500 / month (billed pro-rata for pilot period) OR hourly burst at $38 / GPU-hour

Committed Dedicated Options (post-pilot):
- Dedicated-Small (1x slot): $18,000 / month commitment (recommended if steady-state reranking <500 qps)
- Dedicated-Medium (2x slots): $32,000 / month commitment (recommended if throughput needs exceed 500 qps or to reach <200ms P95 reliably)
- 12-month commit discounts: 10% off listed monthly rates

Notes on hardware and latency:
- For the reranking model and expected long-context behavior, we recommend starting pilot on 1x slot with aggressive KV prefix caching; if P95 doesn't hit target in the initial tuning window, escalate to 2x slots for parallelization and lower tail latency.
- Quantization (4-bit where acceptable) can reduce token cost by ~30% with small quality tradeoffs; we'll propose a canary for the reranking model.

I'll prepare a short one-pager to attach that maps traffic levels to commit tiers and expected P95 ranges.

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
